messages:
maria: FYI starting onboarding thread for cust-aquila LoRA merge on oak-13b-v2.1. Quick-eval pack showed a token id drift and int4 quality regression.
aj: Can you summarize the drift? short bullets pls.
maria: Sure: (1) Their tokenizer introduces 4 specials (<ACCT>,<AMT>,<INVC>,<DATE>) and reassigns several high ids. (2) When we merged adapter weights without reindexing, some currency/punct tokens split into multiple sub-tokens. (3) int4 quant made the downstream extraction EM drop noticeable.
kevin: Any runtime issues after merge?
sara: Saw one kv-cache mismatch when testing long contexts: 
```
RuntimeError: kv_cache size mismatch expected=32 actual=28 at kv_cache.cpp:137
```
Root cause was model.config.max_position_embeddings left at 4096; customer uses 6k contexts. Updated config to 8192 fixed it locally.
yuki: Numbers from quick-eval?
maria: Baseline oak-13b fp16: EM=0.83 F1=0.90
Merged aquila-lora fp16: EM=0.80 F1=0.88
Merged aquila-lora int4 (per-channel): EM=0.74 F1=0.85
So quant is the big delta.
aj: Give 2-3 short failing examples.
sara: Example 1:
input: "Invoice #123 — total $2,450.00"
baseline: "Total: $2,450.00"
merged-int4: "Total 2450.00 dollars"
Example 2:
input: "Acct: 987654 — Due 2025-02-01"
baseline: "Account 987654, Due: 2025-02-01"
merged-int4: "Acct 987654 Due 2025 02 01"
Spacing and punctuation lost.
kevin: Likely tokenization + detokenize spacing rules. Run token diff and share minimal output.
maria: Ran token_diff: `python tools/token_diff.py --ref oak13b --cand merged-int4 samples/cust-aquila.json`
output snippet:
```
$ => base:[2505] mapped:[63,4007]
":" => base:[78] mapped:[78]
"2025-02-01" => base:[1984,12,432] mapped:[1984,12,432]
```
So dollar sign split.
yuki: Two remediation paths: A) enforce base tokenizer + reindex LoRA merges (preferable for exact match), B) add lightweight preprocess mapping that collapses token sequences (like [63,4007] -> $) for production/eval.
aj: For rollout, propose canary fp16 merged variant first + block int4 until we have quant sim/QAT numbers. Agree?
kevin: yes. Also try quant-sim and a tiny QAT run with fake-quant on LoRA params. Use `scripts/qat_sim.py --model merged/aquila-lora --steps 500 --lr 1e-5`.
maria: Kicked a quant sim (per-channel int4 symmetric/asymmetric) and a 500-step QAT sim. eval-bot posted artifacts.
eval-bot: quant_sim results uploaded to /artifacts/aquila/1754450000/quant_sim.json. Per-channel symmetric: EM -0.08; asymmetric: EM -0.05; QAT sim (500 steps) projected EM -0.03.
sara: I pushed a tiny preprocess that normalizes currency tokens and collapses known token splits before detokenize. Reran int4 quickpack: EM improved 0.74 -> 0.77. Better but still below fp16.
yuki: Add token-diff check into quick-eval CI: if any base token maps to >1 token in candidate for >0.1% of samples, flag as token-drift. I can add rule to eval pack.
kevin: Action items: (1) sara/maria: continue token remap patch and collect deterministic tokenized examples; (2) kevin: try a token-aligned LoRA remerge (reindex weights) and run QAT short-run; (3) aj: start fp16 canary (5%) with fallback EM drop >=0.035; (4) yuki: add token-diff check to quickpack + alert.
maria: Filed onboard ticket: https://github.com/redwood-inference/customer-onboards/issues/4339 with diffs, token-dump, and failing samples.
aj: Canary config applied and deploy started. deploy-bot will post when live.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed: aquila-lora-fp16 -> dedicated/pool-9 (5%). Fallback policy: revert to oak-13b when EM_drop >= 0.035 over sliding 1k requests.
kevin: We'll hold int4 rollout pending QAT or remerge + quant-sim that gets EM within threshold. Reopen thread with new artifacts once done. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
